sentences.text:
Deepak Yaduvanshi vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 11
March, 2025
 Neutral Citation No. 2025:Mphc-Jbp:12286
 1 
 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
At Jabalpur

Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Pramod Kumar Agrawal
 On The 11 th Of March, 2025
 Misc. Criminal Case No. 1297 of 2025
 Deepak Yaduvanshi
 Versus
 The State Of Madhya Pradesh And Others
 Appearance:
 Shri Aakash Vishwakarma - Advocate for the applicant.
 Shri Abhay Soni - Advocate for the Objector.

Smt. Sunita Sood - Panel Lawyer for the respondent/Stat
 Order

This is the second application under Section 483 of BNSS for grant of bail in connection with Crime No.172/2024 registered at Police Station Tamiya, District Chhindwara (M.P.) for offence punishable under Sections 376(2)(n), 376(2)(f), 376(3), 506 of IPC and Section 3, 4(2), 5 and 6, of POCSO Act.
The applicant is in custody since 13.11.2024.
First application was dismissed as withdrawn.
2. As per the prosecution story, allegations against the applicant is that he alongwith other co-accused has abducted the minor prosecutrix and committed rape upon her.
On the basis of which, the offence has been registered against the applicant and co-accused under aforesaid sections.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case.
The incident of the year 2019 but F.I.R. was lodged on 24.10.2024 and in the F.I.R. name of present applicant is not mentioned.

It is further submitted that video of the incident has been seized and NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:12286 2 MCRC-1297-2025 except it no articles has been recovered from the mobile of co-accused Golu and he has already been enlarged on bail by this Hon'ble Court in MCRC No.51558 of 2024.
Charge-sheet has been filed.
There are no criminal antecedents of the applicant.
The conclusion of the trial will take considerable time, therefore, it has been prayed that the applicant may be released on bail.

sentences.text: On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondent/State as well as counsel for the Objector have opposed the bail application and prayed for it's rejection.
5. Having taken into consideration all the facts and circumstances of the case, but without commenting on merit of the case, I am inclined to release the applicant on bail.
Consequently, bail application under Section 483 of BNSS for grant of bail filed on behalf of applicant, stands allowed.

6. It is directed that applicant be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, for his regular appearance before the trial Court during trial with a condition that he shall remain present before the concerned Court on all the dates fixed by it during trial.
He shall abide by all the conditions enumerated under Section 480(3) of BNSS.
7. This order shall be effective till the end of the trial.
However, in case of bail jump and breach of any of the conditions of bail, it shall become ineffective.
Certified copy as per rules.

(PRAMOD KUMAR AGRAWAL) JUDGE SN Deepak Yaduvanshi vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 11 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34165263/
